claim: NVIDIA launched an open agent-safety platform that places enforceable boundaries and out-of-band monitoring below the agent application layer.
verifiedFacts: NVIDIA announced Open Agent Safety Platform on September 28.
OpenShell enforces runtime boundaries and traces actions; Sentry monitors externally and can quarantine agents.
NVIDIA says more than 100 organizations are participating.
inference: Seed Loom should remain vendor-neutral and test evidence across model safeguards, harness permissions, runtime enforcement and independent monitoring.

Consultancy implication: agent-boundary audits can be sold as a layered control review rather than a generic governance workshop. Project disposition: Seed Loom CORE; agent-runtime-control-center PRODUCTIZE if bounded to evidence/attention/reconciliation.
significance: Very high: runtime enforcement is being productized as a separate infrastructure layer.
assumptions: The partner ecosystem will mature into deployable controls.
knownLimitations: Vendor claims lack independent production benchmarks.
